suggestions.title: Define Quantitative Deviation Thresholds
suggestions.detail: The current SOP relies on 'judgement' to determine significance of deviations. This introduces inconsistency. Defining a quantitative threshold (e.g., +/- 10% variance) ensures objective reporting.
suggestions.proposed_text: Identify any metrics that deviate from the target or prior period by more than 10%. Deviations exceeding this threshold must be logged and investigated.

suggestions.title: Mandate Evidence Retention for Audit Trail
suggestions.detail: The SOP describes data collection but does not explicitly require functional teams to provide or store the primary source evidence (e.g., utility bills) in a central repository, which is critical for the 'BRSR Core' assurance mentioned in Section 3.
suggestions.proposed_text: Teams should provide data in the agreed format, accompanied by primary source evidence (e.g., PDF of utility bills, system-generated reports, or certificates). All evidence must be uploaded to the central ESG Data Repository for audit purposes.
suggestions.original_text: Teams should provide data in the agreed format and by the agreed deadline

suggestions.title: Standardize Reporting Timelines
suggestions.detail: The SOP mentions 'agreed deadlines' but does not provide a standard timeframe (e.g., T+10 days after quarter end). Standardizing this prevents delays in consolidated reporting.
suggestions.proposed_text: Teams should provide data in the agreed format no later than 10 working days following the end of the reporting period (Quarterly or Annual).
suggestions.original_text: Teams should provide data in the agreed format and by the agreed deadline
